logline: A minor god hustling for prayers and a girl whose soul keeps slipping out of her body make an unlikely partnership navigating the border between the living world and the afterlife.

renewal.note: Two seasons aired (2014, 2015). No third season announced as of 2026; the manga by Adachitoka concluded, and Bones has not greenlit further adaptation.

bollymeter.basis: Noragami's first season earns its reputation as solid, all-around entertainment: Bones animates the supernatural action with flair, and the god-shinki mythology gives the show genuine texture. IMDb aggregate sits at 7.8.

seasons.review_body: Noragami's first season aired on MBS from January to March 2014, adapting Adachitoka's manga through Bones studio. Critics described it as 'solid, all-around, well-constructed entertainment' - a show that blends Shinto mythology, supernatural action, and adolescent longing without overreaching. The three-way dynamic between Yato (a gods-for-hire deity), Hiyori (a girl straddling life and death), and Yukine (a troubled weapon spirit) gives the season genuine emotional stakes. IGN later included it among the best anime of the 2010s. The season functions as a strong introduction arc, though some critics noted it ends before the manga's deeper conflicts emerge.

episode_reviews.title: A Housecat, a Stray God, and a Tail
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Yato as a minor deity advertising his services on bathroom stalls, willing to grant any wish for five yen. The tone is established fast - comic irreverence over genuine supernatural menace - and Hiyori's accident into the spirit world gives the premise its hook.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Yato's business card handed out at a crosswalk - the perfect image of divine underachievement.

episode_reviews.title: To Cut, or Not to Cut
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale confronts the conflict between Yato and Yukine that has been building since the midpoint. The emotional resolution lands harder than the action, grounding a supernatural climax in something that reads as genuine grief about belonging and purpose.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The ritual that forces Yato's hand - the season's moral weight finally made physical.

bollymeter.basis: Noragami Aragoto deepens the mythology and raises the emotional stakes considerably over Season 1; Anime News Network's Theron Martin rated it 4.5 out of 5, citing its 'captivating art design and powerful depth of emotion.'

pull_quotes.text: With its captivating art design, lovable characters, and powerful depth of emotion, Noragami Aragoto is bound to be an enjoyable experience.

seasons.review_body: Noragami Aragoto aired from October to December 2015 on MBS, covering arcs that expand Bishamon's backstory and introduce the god Ebisu. Critics responded more warmly to this season than the first: Anime News Network's review called it a considerable step up, with art design and emotional depth that match the stronger source material. The Bishamon arc in particular - examining the poisoned bond between a war god and her unstable shinki - gave the season a tragic weight the first season only gestures toward. The mean AniList score of 80 and the critical consensus around emotional resonance place this firmly as the show's peak.
seasons.season_over_season: Aragoto graduates from promising setup to emotionally complex mythology, with the Bishamon arc delivering the dramatic payoff Season 1 builds toward.

episode_reviews.title: Slay
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint episode where the Bishamon arc reaches its breaking point. The cost of devotion - how a god's refusal to release troubled shinki poisons everyone around them - is rendered with unusual precision for a shonen-adjacent series.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The revelation of what Bishamon has been protecting, and what it has cost her.
